newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-I'LL BE BACK, SAYS OUTCAST BAGGIO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-I'LL BE BACK, SAYS OUTCAST BAGGIO.

text.p: Idle idol Roberto Baggio told the world of soccer not to write him off on Friday.
He vowed to win back a place in Italy's line-up and return to regular play for AC Milan, where he is now an expensive reserve, and said he had no intention of moving abroad.
The 29-year-old "Divine Ponytail", world player of the year in 1993 and Italy's hero in the World Cup in 1994, has not played for his country since September 1995.
He told Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper in an interview that he had "not even dreamed" of never returning to the national side despite his long absence.

"I am the leading national goalscorer still playing," said Baggio. "I've scored 24 goals and I'm not 30 yet so why should I give up? No. It's still on my mind and I'm going to do everything to return."

He said the same ambition applied at league champions AC Milan, where he has lost a regular place to striking duo Liberian George Weah and Marco Simone. Baggio is expected to be on the bench again on Saturday, when Milan travel to Roma.

"I still train and behave as if I were playing every weekend and every game. You know what the problem is? Just one. If I were a foreigner nobody, or very few people, would have laid into me so heavily," Baggio said.
He said he would not think of his future until his contract with Milan, which he signed in 1995, expired next year but a move abroad was out of the question.
"Never. I don't even want to think about it," Baggio said. "I'm not interested".
